Āryabhaṭa
I. jy. of Kusumapura; born A.

; wrote in 499.
--Āryabhaṭīya. jy. Comprising the Daśagītikāsūtra (10-13 āryās) on numerical notation an. the Āryāṣṭaśata (108 āryās) in 3 pādas: gaṇita, kālakriyā an. gola. Some mss. an. commentators take the two parts a. two separate works. Probably wrote another, a Karaṇa work, dated 505 A.D., which has not yet come to light, but the substance of which is contained in the Khaṇḍakhādya of Brahmagupta. See Dikshit, Ind. Ant. XIX. p.. 45-54; Bhāratīya Jyotiṣa, p. 273, Hindi version; Sengupta, Dept. of Letters, Cal. Uni., XVIII. p.. 2-3 of his paper; On Āryabhaṭa I an. II an. their works, see Bull. Cal. Math. Soc.

Āryarakṣitasūri
Jain. of Kharataragaccha; son of Somadeva; ref. to in Jain literature a. one who knew nine of the Pūrvas; his story told in Āvaśyakacūrṇī (p.. I. p.. 397-415); said to have passed away in Vīra saṁ. 584 or 597. See Ind. Ant. XI. p. 247; Peters. III. App. p. 308; Kapadia, Can. Lit. of the Jainas, p.. 52-53, 73. For his story, see Prabhāvakacarita, story no. 2. The supposition that Anuyogadvārasūtra is his work is wrong. See Kapadia, ibid. p. 161.
